products.title: Ishtar Goddess Pendant
products.body_html:
Queen of Heaven. The earliest known deity. Goddess of war, love and sex. Ishtar's power is ancient and mysterious — civilization's first embodiment of the divine feminine in all its complexities. Ishtar ventured to the Underworld to learn its secrets, passing through the inner chambers of death before being reborn when her husband's life was traded for her own. Her journey became the archetype for all stories of descent that followed, but she ventured into the darkness not for love, but for wisdom. Her complexity is depicted in silver and gold: naked at the moment of her ascent back from the depths, flanked by her lions, a symbol of regal dominion, and owls, her guardians of the night. Wear her as a reminder to seek knowledge for knowledge's sake, hold complete authority over your own life, and never fear the dark, even when it changes you.

For each piece sold, $10 will be donated to an organization fighting to support LGBTQ+ youth at a time when funding is most needed.

products.title: Special Edition Circe Pendant
products.body_html: Goddess of magic, metamorphoses, and potions, Circe was feared and revered for her sorcery. Her ability to transmute humans into animals made her a fearsome figure in the Odyssey, but other tales reflect the true breadth of her talents: casting illusions to block out the sun, communing with the dead, and concocting potions that could heal or damn. Set on a stunning slab of moonstone for intuition and feminine powers, she confidently waves a wand over a goblet containing her latest tincture. Animals from her menagerie (perhaps once human) rest by her sides. Wear Circe to embrace all the hidden powers inside you, even — and especially — those that others whisper about.

products.title: Oshun Goddess Pendant
products.body_html:
Through her, all things flow. In Yoruba belief, Oshun is the Orisha of beauty, sensuality, and rivers. Presiding over desire and destiny, she consults her mirror not as a form of vanity, but as an act of deep self-knowledge. Her pendant depicts her draped in finery and crowned in a cascade of waves, invoking abundance. White sapphires ring her pendant, and the symbol for water is inscribed on the back. Wear Oshun when you need a reminder to adorn yourself intentionally, or when the situation calls for using sweetness as a strategy.

products.title: Special Edition Lilith Signet Ring
products.body_html:
Long ago, Lilith was Adam's first wife in the Garden of Eden. When she refused to submit to his desires, she was banished, demonized and called a succubus. products.title: Sekhmet & Bastet Dual Goddess Pendant
products.body_html: Ancient feline intelligence meets feminine duality. In ancient Egypt, Sekhmet was the lion-headed Goddess of war and medicine, both feared and respected. In contrast to her fire-breathing, warlike ways, her sister Bastet is Goddess of the home and protector of women and children, embodied by the domestic housecat. Together, they represent the full spectrum of divine femininity — and wearing their twin symbols makes space for the duality within you. Flip the Goddess pendant to wear Sekhmet facing outward when the world requires your ferocity and strength, or wear Bastet to reveal your softer side. Emeralds (for wisdom) and blue sapphires (for intuition) surround these revered Goddesses and call in what you need.

products.title: Special Edition Medusa Cameo
products.body_html:
History's most recognizable protective symbol, rendered in the world's most time-honored jewelry tradition. Since Ancient Greece, cameos have been hand-carved from precious stones, revealing public figures or mythic monsters in the reliefs. As a decorative element on shields or architectural carvings, Medusa's furious face was believed to ward off misfortune. Reimagined with a Victorian "openwork" halo of serpents, her power is not just protective but instructive: a reminder that your ferocity is not something to apologize for. It may be the source of your power.

For each piece sold, $10 will be donated to a support survivors of sexual violence through our partnerships with leading organizations in this space.

The symbol of a snake consuming its own tail is no less powerful now, even — and especially — when its tail cradles an energetic gemstone. Choose white sapphire to call in wisdom, or red garnet to ignite inner passions. Both stones bring their own power to this timeless protective talisman.

products.title: Real-Life Goddess Pendant
products.body_html:
Their circumstances made them real; their decisions made them Goddesses. The Real-Life Goddesses capsule honors the historic women whose courage, creativity, and conviction embody divine strength in human form. Seven iconic names that echo through history, immortalized in modern heirlooms. Each pendant is finished with a white sapphire star on the reverse side, and is engraved with the name of the Real-Life Goddess it pays tribute to. Honor their lives; channel their power.

For each piece sold, $10 will be donated to an organization supporting women's initiatives that aligns with the Real-Life Goddess's life and work.

Jane Austen: Keen critic of society, author of the modern literary heroine. Wear her to move through life with creativity, wisdom and wonder at the world around you — and to see through society's posturing with a sharp wit and an astute eye. Inscription reads: "Indulge your imagination in every possible flight. — Jane Austen"

Joan of Arc: Sainted warrior, savior of France. Wear her to channel her unwavering conviction and strengthen your self-belief. Inscription reads: "I am not afraid, I was born to do this. — Joan of Arc"

Cleopatra: Powerful strategist, the last queen of Egypt. Wear her to embody self-sovereignty and cleverly navigate obstacles with divine vision. Inscribed with Cleopatra's name on the reverse.

Frida Kahlo: Visionary artist, guardian of the revolution. Wear her to design your own destiny, craft a life without labels, and leave your indelible image on the world around you. Inscription reads: "I am the person I know best. — Frida Kahlo"

Sacajawea: Native American emissary, navigator of the new world. Wear her to access expansive inner knowledge and explore without boundaries. Inscribed with Sacajawea's name on the reverse.

Harriet Tubman: Leader of liberation, engineer of the Underground Railroad. Wear her to channel radical empathy, discover strength in the face of injustice, and architect a shared liberation. Inscription reads: "Every great dream begins with a dreamer. — Harriet Tubman"

Marie Curie: Two-time Nobel Prize winner, mother of modern physics. Wear her to ignite lifelong curiosity, inspire a drive toward discovery, and break barriers to attain your highest achievements. Inscription reads: "The way of progress is neither swift nor easy. — Marie Curie"

Marsha P. Johnson: Queer activist, the saint of Christopher Street. Wear her to stand tall in the face of oppression, to live freely without shame, and to show your full self to the world. Inscription reads: "Pay it no mind. — Marsha P. Johnson"
